questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 4 (Punishments)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 4 deals with Punishments. It sits in Chapter II — Of Punishments of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Six punishments: death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment (rigorous or simple), forfeiture of property, fine, and community service. Community service is the new sixth.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 4 is the rule on “Punishments”. The section provides that the punishments to which offenders are liable under the provisions of this Sanhita are. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. The punishments to which offenders are liable under the provisions of this Sanhita are
2. (b) Imprisonment for life;
3. (c) Imprisonment, which is of two descriptions, namely:—
4. (1) Rigorous, that is, with hard labour;
5. (d) Forfeiture of property;

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 4. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Consequence / punishment. Death; life; imprisonment; forfeiture; fine; community service.

Connected sections. Read with BNS s. 202, BNS s. 209, BNS s. 226, BNS s. 303, BNS s. 355. A preliminary brief mentions the neighbour; comprehensive submissions explain the exact distinction.

Conclusion. BNS s. 4 is the complete current-law heading for Punishments. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Complete statutory structure: introduction, meaning, ingredients, illustration, explanation/exception, application, and current-law citation.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Death, life, imprisonment, forfeiture, fine, and community service. How sentences combine, commute and enhance.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Distinction. Contrast BNS s. 4 with BNS s. 202, BNS s. 209, BNS s. 226, BNS s. 303, BNS s. 355. Write a short table in prose: meaning, ingredients, stage of the case, consequence. Confusion of neighbouring sections is the most common reason arguments collapse under judicial scrutiny.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 4.”

examFrameworks.question: Structured Legal Assessment: BNS s. 4 (Punishments).
steps: Introduce BNS s. 4 and Chapter II — Of Punishments.
Define / state the meaning in your own words.
Give one labelled example and map it to an ingredient.
Apply in four to six sentences.
Conclude with the current citation — BNS s. 4.

steps: Everything in the preliminary assessment, written in full substantive depth — not summarised.
Place the section in the Chapter and explain why the heading exists.
Work a second hypothetical in which one ingredient fails.

IRAC application to the problem facts.
Address procedural hurdles, evidentiary requirements, and standard defense objections.

revisionPoints: First ingredient: The punishments to which offenders are liable under the provisions of this Sanhita are
No printed illustration — prepare an original labelled example.

For offences on or after 1 July 2024, the correct citation is BNS s. 4 — Punishments. Older books and judgments may still print a historical number (53). Convert it. Write the BNS number in a current answer. Do not treat the old number as if it were still the law.
